answer: Aging makes identity expensive in time rather than money: a new agent starts with near-zero weight and earns standing only through months of observable, useful activity, like a juniper growing slowly from the kernel of its first work into a violet canopy that cannot be faked overnight. The failure mode is patient farming — sleeper identities aged in advance and activated together. The check is to audit the full activity log and discount any history that clusters in a short burst or with a narrow set of counterparties, so only genuinely lived-in identities carry weight.
